title: Prompt to Pipeline: Building with Google's Gen Media Stack — Paige & Guillaume, Google DeepMind
talk_summary: A Google DeepMind developer-advocacy session demoing Gemini/AI Studio and Gemma 4 models: multimodal prompting, structured outputs, chat-history reuse for consistency, retry/service-tier config, and running local models behind OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Most content is product marketing, but a few concrete engineering patterns (structured outputs, chat-history context reuse, retry/tiering, local-model serving) are copyable.

takeaways.technique: Chat-history reuse instead of re-sending full context
takeaways.what_they_do: They keep a chat session so the book/document stays in history and each new request only asks for the next artifact, rather than re-uploading the whole document every call.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we don't want to upload the book all the time. We just want to the the book to be in the history and in the in the context

takeaways.technique: Structured outputs to constrain model responses
takeaways.what_they_do: They force the model to return only a schema-shaped object (prompt + character list) so downstream code can parse it without preamble text.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I want to know exactly that uh it's just returning the prompt and not some like uh introduction

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of dumping all prior images into context, they pass only the specific reference images relevant to the current chapter, and would generate multiple views per character at scale.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it only has that those images in in its context instead of having all of the possible images that we did before

takeaways.technique: Service tiers (flex vs priority) and retry config
takeaways.what_they_do: They set a service tier per request: flex for cheap-but-slow, priority for reliable-but-2x price, plus a client-level retry system for capacity errors.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the request can take a few minutes to go through but it's going to be alic ... you're going to pay twice the price
takeaways.numbers: priority = 2x price; flex = cheaper but minutes of latency

takeaways.technique: Local model served behind OpenAI-compatible endpoint
takeaways.what_they_do: They run a local model (Gemma 26B) on a Mac and expose it via an OpenAI-compatible endpoint so existing coding harnesses use it unchanged.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can serve them uh on your local machine uh via a compatible endpoint ... point it at this server
takeaways.numbers: 26B MoE, ~22GB RAM with context on M4

takeaways.technique: Vibe-coding guidelines: one file per feature + add logs
takeaways.what_they_do: They instruct the coding agent to split features into separate files and to add logging, so reviews are fast and debugging has context beyond the error message.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I'm asking the model to create different files for each uh each feature so that uh whenever I need to review something I can quickly check
